findings.title: No test fails when the unsettled delta check of unlock is removed, and under the --isolate flag of the CI no test pins the lock close or the reset of the synced currency; the source has all three statements
findings.difference: None. This is a property of the repository's tests and it is the same on every network. The network features that each unpinned statement stands against are named in the mechanism field.
findings.mechanism: I read every guard and accounting statement in the assigned lines together with every test under test/ and every helper under src/test, and asked which test fails when the statement is removed or its condition is inverted. Nothing could be compiled, so the answer comes from reading. Three statements carry the whole custody model and are weakly pinned. First, src/PoolManager.sol:112 reverts with CurrencyNotSettled when the count of nonzero deltas is not zero at the end of unlock. No file under test/ names CurrencyNotSettled. Outside the interface and PoolManager.sol the name occurs only in the copy of unlock at src/test/ProxyPoolManager.sol:66. Every expectRevert that is reached through a router expects another error, and the bare expectRevert at test/PoolManager.t.sol:917-922 is satisfied by the failing token transfer. Inverting the condition fails every test that completes an unlock. Removing the line fails no test. The line is what makes take, mint and a swap output a loan that must be repaid (A5), and it reads a transient counter (A1). Second, src/PoolManager.sol:113 closes the lock. Without --isolate the second unlock of one test transaction would revert with AlreadyUnlocked, for example in the setup helper at test/utils/Deployers.sol:199-211, which adds liquidity twice. The CI runs forge test --isolate (.github/workflows/tests-pr.yml:37, .github/workflows/tests-merge.yml:31), and in that mode every top level call of a test is its own transaction, so transient storage is empty at the next call and no test notices a lock that stays open. I found no test that performs two unlocks inside one top level call and no assertion that the manager is locked after an unlock returns. Third, src/PoolManager.sol:361 resets the synced currency after a token settle. Without the reset a second settle would credit the same balance rise again, because the stored reserves are not updated. test_settle_twice_doesNotApplyDelta (test/Sync.t.sol:341-374) does not detect that: it takes the credited amount between the two settles, so the balance equals the stored reserves again and the second settle pays zero with or without the reset, and its last assertion reads the delta of address(0), which is zero in both cases. Without --isolate the reset is pinned by the setup helper, where a token settle is followed by a native settle with value in the same transaction and a stale token sync would raise NonzeroNativeValue (test/utils/Deployers.sol:203-206, src/PoolManager.sol:356). With --isolate nothing pins it. Further statements that no test pins in either mode: the onlyWhenUnlocked modifier on settleFor and on clear (src/PoolManager.sol:305, 310; the locked tests cover take, settle, mint and burn at test/PoolManager.t.sol:962-999); the toInt128 limit as applied in take, clear, mint, burn and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:294, 313, 326, 334, 364; the library function is pinned by test/libraries/SafeCast.t.sol:85-99, and no manager test uses an amount of 2^127 or more); the use of _burnFrom with its allowance and operator check in burn (src/PoolManager.sol:335; the check is pinned on the mock at test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol:15-48, and every manager test sets the router as operator before it burns); the truncation of the id in mint and burn (src/PoolManager.sol:324, 333); the checked subtraction for a balance that fell between sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:360); the acceptance of empty return data, the minimum of 32 bytes for a returned value and the absence of a code check in the token transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74; the tests use tokens that return true, a token that returns false and a contract that reverts); the amount of gas forwarded with a native payout (src/types/Currency.sol:48); the minimum of 32 bytes for a hook answer and the exact 64 bytes for a hook that returns a delta (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152, 166; the mock hooks always return full words); and the absence of a lock check in collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, recorded in F-006 and F-014). For the increment branch at src/PoolManager.sol:375 I found no test that moves one delta from a nonzero value to another nonzero value and then asserts the count; I did not trace every hook test for that case. I then read each of these statements as if it were the only changed line. Each does what its comment, its error name and the surrounding tests require: line 112 reads NonzeroDeltaCount and runs before the lock is closed; line 113 writes false to the lock slot; line 361 writes zero to the currency slot after the balance was read and before the delta is booked; take, mint and clear negate a value that toInt128 has limited to 2^127 - 1 and book it to msg.sender; burn credits msg.sender and burns from the named account through _burnFrom; settleFor credits the recipient. The deployed PoolManagers are other bytecode than a build of this checkout, so a read-only test of them says how each network executes these paths and nothing about this build. With that limit, three eth_call probes with a forwarder stub placed by state override gave the same words on all 21 networks, the Unichain predeploy included: a callback that only mints leaves the unlock reverting with 0x5212cba1 (CurrencyNotSettled); the lock slot reads zero and a take reverts with ManagerLocked right after unlock returns in the same call; the currency slot reads the synced address before settle and zero after it; settleFor, clear, settle, take, mint and burn revert with ManagerLocked outside an unlock; amounts of 2^127 revert with SafeCastOverflow in mint, take and burn; a burn of claims that another address holds does not credit the caller.
findings.impact: No funds are at risk from the source as it is written. The observation matters for the review method: a build in which line 112 is missing would let any account take every token without paying, a build without line 113 would let any call that follows an unlock in the same transaction take without an end check, and a build without line 361 would let one payment be credited twice, and the repository's tests as the CI runs them would pass in all three cases. Earlier cycles relied on the tests to confirm the source. For these statements the confirmation comes from reading the text and, for the deployed contracts only, from the probes.
findings.preconditions: None for the observation itself. A loss would need a build in which one of the listed statements is missing or changed. The text of this checkout shows each statement in place, and nobody in this review could compile it.
findings.mitigations: Before deployment, compile this checkout and run the three probes in research/network-risk/cycles/006/core-code-test-pins.work against the built bytecode placed at a test address by state override on each network, or add tests: an unlock whose callback leaves a debt must revert with CurrencyNotSettled; a take right after an unlock in the same call must revert with ManagerLocked; two settles in a row after one payment must credit once; settleFor and clear must revert while locked; a burn by an account without approval must revert at the manager.

sources.supports: The end check of unlock: reverts with CurrencyNotSettled when NonzeroDeltaCount is not zero.
The lock is closed after the end check.
A token settle credits the balance rise since sync and then resets the synced currency.
test_settle_twice_doesNotApplyDelta takes the credited amount between two settles and asserts the delta of address(0), so it passes with or without the reset.
The setup helper adds token liquidity and then native liquidity with value, which pins lines 113 and 361 only when the whole setup is one transaction.
The CI command is forge test --isolate -vvv. The same command is at .github/workflows/tests-merge.yml:31.
Fetched 2026-11-23. Lines 145-151 document the isolate option: in isolation mode all top level calls are executed as a separate transaction in a separate EVM context.
The nested unlock test expects AlreadyUnlocked inside a callback. No test asserts that the manager is locked after unlock returns.
Locked tests exist for take, settle, mint and burn. None exists for settleFor or clear.
The allowance and operator check of _burnFrom is tested on MockERC6909Claims only.

sources.supports: All 21 deployed PoolManagers answered the same: CurrencyNotSettled after a callback that only mints, ManagerLocked for a take right after unlock returned, synced currency zero after settle, SafeCastOverflow for 2^127, ManagerLocked for settleFor and clear outside an unlock. Example blocks: Ethereum 26478014, 26478031 and 26478042; Unichain 64690717, 64690913 and 64691062.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114): which test fails for each line, and does each line do what its comment and error name say.
cleared.result: Line 105 rejects a second unlock and is pinned by test_unlock_cannotBeCalledTwiceByCaller and test_unlock_cannotBeCalledTwiceByDifferentCallers (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1181-1189) through the expectRevert at src/test/PoolNestedActionsTest.sol:60 and 113. Line 107 opens the lock and is pinned by every test that acts inside a callback, since take, swap and the others would revert with ManagerLocked. Line 110 calls unlockCallback on msg.sender and returns its bytes; test_unlock_EmitsCorrectId (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1173-1177) pins the call and the routers that decode the returned delta pin the bytes (src/test/PoolSwapTest.sol:40-42). Line 112 is pinned against inversion only, and line 113 only without --isolate; both are in the finding of this file. The order is check, then lock. unlock is not payable and carries no noDelegateCall, which earlier cycles recorded. Each line matches its comment and error name.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of sync, take, settle, settleFor and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-307, 349-365): operators, sign of the delta, the address the delta is booked to, order of the transient write and the external call, and the slot that is read or reset.
cleared.result: sync: the native branch resets the currency slot only (line 283), pinned by test_settle_native_afterERC20Sync_succeeds (test/Sync.t.sol:300-339), where a native settle after sync(address(0)) must succeed. The token branch stores currency and balance (lines 285-286), pinned by test_sync_balanceIsNonzero and test_sync_multiple_unlocked (test/Sync.t.sol:36-80). The absence of a lock check is pinned by the tests that call sync directly on a locked manager (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1023, test/Sync.t.sol:36-41). take: line 294 books minus amount to msg.sender, pinned by the delta of -10 in test_settle_nonNative_withoutSync_loseFunds (test/Sync.t.sol:220-225), by the pranked taker in test_settle_payOnBehalf (test/Sync.t.sol:130-158) and by src/test/PoolTakeTest.sol:48; line 295 pays the named recipient, pinned by src/test/PoolTakeTest.sol:50-57; the lock guard by test_take_failsIfLocked. settle books to msg.sender and settleFor to the recipient, pinned by test_settle_twice_doesNotApplyDelta (delta equals value) and test_settle_payOnBehalf (the taker's delta returns to zero). _settle: line 353 takes msg.value when no token is synced, pinned by the native delta assertion at test/Sync.t.sol:331-332; line 356 uses msg.value > 0 and is pinned by test_settle_revertsSendingNative_withTokenSynced (test/PoolManager.t.sol:976-989) and test_settle_failsWithNativeERC20IfNotSyncedInOrder (test/Sync.t.sol:255-277); lines 358-360 read the reserves slot and the live balance and subtract with a checked subtraction, pinned for a rise by the clear and sync tests and unpinned for a fall; line 361 resets the currency slot (see the finding); line 364 books plus paid through toInt128. Every statement reads or writes the slot its name says, and every sign agrees with the tests: a payout is negative, a payment positive.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of clear, mint, burn and _accountDelta (src/PoolManager.sol:310-336, 368-378).
cleared.result: clear reads the delta of msg.sender, converts the amount with toInt128, requires equality and books the negated amount; the five revert tests and the exact case pin the comparison and the sign (test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol:18-190). clear(0) with a zero delta is accepted and pinned (test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol:114-135), although the error name says positive. mint debits msg.sender and credits the claim to the named address under the truncated id; test_swap_mint6909IfOutputNotTaken_gas pins the receiver, the id, the amount and the Transfer event (test/PoolManager.t.sol:659-670), and the debit is pinned because the router's positive delta must close. burn credits msg.sender and burns from the named account through _burnFrom; test_swap_burn6909AsInput_gas pins the amounts and the event with the router as operator (test/PoolManager.t.sol:690-716). The lock guards of mint and burn are pinned (test/PoolManager.t.sol:991-999); the guard of clear is not. _accountDelta: the early return for zero is pinned by the count assertion of test_clear_zeroDelta_inputZero_isUnchanged, because without it a zero delta on an empty slot would decrement the count; the decrement on reaching zero and the increment on leaving zero are pinned by the counts 1 and 0 in test_clear_positiveDelta_inputExact_succeeds (test/PoolManager.clear.t.sol:156-190). The unchecked blocks in take, clear and mint cover only the negation of a value below 2^127; the called functions keep their own checked arithmetic.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of the transfer and balance functions (src/types/Currency.sol:40-96).
cleared.result: Native branch: CALL with all gas, the amount as value and empty calldata (line 48), failure wrapped in NativeTransferFailed (lines 51-53); test_fuzz_transfer_native pins the amounts and the revert (test/types/Currency.t.sol:138-159). The gas amount is unpinned: the only native recipients in the tests are test contracts with an empty receive function. Token branch: selector 0xa9059cbb, which I recomputed from transfer(address,uint256), the recipient masked to 160 bits, the amount at offset 36 and a call of 68 bytes (lines 60-73); test_fuzz_transfer_token pins the movement and the bubbled arithmetic error (test/types/Currency.t.sol:161-184), test_transfer_noReturnData pins a revert without data (test/types/Currency.t.sol:122-136), and test_take_failsWithInvalidTokensThatDoNotReturnTrueOnTransfer pins the rejection of a returned false (test/PoolManager.t.sol:924-956). Unpinned: success with empty return data, the 32 byte minimum for a returned value, and the absence of a code check, all of which belong to assumption A4 and were judged in earlier cycles (F-054). balanceOfSelf reads the native balance for address(0) and balanceOf(address(this)) otherwise, pinned by test/types/Currency.t.sol:46-62. balanceOf is declared view (src/interfaces/external/IERC20Minimal.sol:10), so sync and settle read it through a static call. The code matches the comment at lines 66-67.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57).
cleared.result: Line 48 (caller must be the controller) is pinned by test_collectProtocolFees_revertsWithInvalidCaller (test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.t.sol:100-103). Lines 49-52 (synced token) are pinned by three tests, locked and unlocked (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1039). The exemption of address(0) in line 49 is pinned by test_collectProtocolFees_nativeToken_accumulateFees_gas (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1120-1145): the currency slot reads zero when nothing is synced, so without the exemption every native collection would revert. Line 54 (zero means all) is pinned by the two returnsAllFees tests, line 55 (checked decrement) by test_fuzz_collectProtocolFees (test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.t.sol:117-147), line 56 by the recipient balance assertions. Unpinned: the order of decrement and transfer, and the missing lock check that src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 describes (F-006, F-014). The function needs the fee controller, so none of this is open to an ordinary account. On the eight networks with a controller (chain ids 1, 10, 8453, 42161, 4663, 137, 56, 5042) a stub placed at the controller address by state override received ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced (0xc79e5948) from the deployed PoolManager for a collection of the synced currency inside an unlock.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of the claim token functions (src/ERC6909.sol:25-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22).
cleared.result: transfer debits msg.sender and credits the receiver with checked arithmetic, pinned by testTransfer and the underflow and overflow tests (test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol:81-93, 151-174). transferFrom skips the allowance for the owner and for an operator, leaves an unlimited allowance unchanged and otherwise subtracts with a checked subtraction; pinned by testTransferFromWithApproval, testTransferFromWithInfiniteApproval, testTransferFromAsOperator and test_revertTransferFromNotAuthorized (test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol:95-143, 201-209). The mapping order is owner then operator, and owner then spender then id, in the declarations, in setOperator and approve, and in both readers. _burnFrom applies the same rule with msg.sender as spender and is pinned by test_burnFrom_withApproval and test_burnFrom_revertsWithNoApproval (test/ERC6909Claims.t.sol:15-48); its operator branch is pinned through the manager tests that set the router as operator (test/PoolManager.t.sol:346-374, 690-716). The interface id 0x0f632fb3 equals the XOR of the seven ERC-6909 selectors, which I recomputed. A transferFrom of amount zero by an unapproved caller succeeds and moves nothing.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of the hook address check and the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-175).
cleared.result: Lines 111-120 reject a return delta flag without its action flag, pinned by test_fuzz_isValidHookAddress_invalid_returnsDeltaWithoutHookFlag (test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:962-972). Lines 124-126 are pinned by the literal address tests at test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:940-990, which include bit 13 as valid and bit 14 alone as invalid. Lines 131-137: CALL with all gas and no value; a failed call is wrapped with the hook address and the selector, pinned by test_callHook_revertsWithBubbleUp and test_callHook_revertsWithInternalErrorFailedHookCall (test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:992-1045). Lines 140-149 copy the return data. Line 152 compares the first word with the selector sent; the ten invalidReturn tests pin the comparison (test/libraries/Hooks.t.sol:55-65, 110-141, 156-169, 178-188). Unpinned: the 32 byte minimum in line 152 and the exact 64 bytes in line 166, because src/test/MockHooks.sol always returns full words. As written, an answer shorter than 32 bytes is rejected, so an address without code or a precompile that returns nothing cannot pass as a hook, which earlier cycles tested on chain. noSelfCall (lines 171-175) is pinned by the counter assertions in test/SkipCallsTestHook.t.sol:42-75. The comment at line 136 names the error FailedHookCall while the code uses HookCallFailed.

cleared.check: Pin list and second reading of the four transient slot libraries, with the constants recomputed (src/libraries/Lock.sol, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol, CurrencyReserves.sol, CurrencyDelta.sol).
cleared.result: With a local Keccak I recomputed keccak256 of Unlocked, NonzeroDeltaCount, ReservesOf and Currency minus one; all four equal the constants in the source, and each has a test that states the same (test/libraries/Lock.t.sol:20-22, test/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.t.sol:43-45, test/CurrencyReserves.t.sol:43-49). Lock writes true and false to its slot and reads it (test/libraries/Lock.t.sol:8-18). NonzeroDeltaCount adds and subtracts one on its slot (test/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.t.sol:8-41). CurrencyReserves writes the masked currency and the value to their two slots, reset writes zero to the currency slot only, and the readers load the matching slots (test/CurrencyReserves.t.sol:17-57). CurrencyDelta hashes the target at offset 0 and the currency at offset 32, the same layout as the reader in src/libraries/TransientStateLibrary.sol:35-43 that the tests use for every delta assertion, and adds with checked arithmetic. Every mask of an address in these files has 40 hex digits. No statement reads or resets a slot other than the one its name says.

cleared.check: Behaviour of the 21 deployed PoolManagers at the statements that no test pins, read-only. A forwarder stub was placed at 0x66c94e9dcddb7723cbf6d6b7aa85fa0bd619c52a by state override. Called by an outside sender it forwards the calldata to the PoolManager; called by the PoolManager it runs the inner calls passed in the unlock data and returns their success flags and first return words. The claim id was the address 0xb01b749eb983d41e87c2dc1f975774bc526b52e3, which has no code on any of the 21 networks.
cleared.result: All 21 endpoints returned the same words, the 24,050 byte Unichain predeploy included. Outside an unlock, settleFor, clear, settle, take, mint and burn revert with 0x54e3ca0d (ManagerLocked) and sync(address(0)) succeeds. mint to the stub followed by burn from the stub: unlock succeeds. mint only: unlock reverts with 0x5212cba1 (CurrencyNotSettled). mint to a third address followed by burn from that address by the unapproved stub: unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled, so the burn gave no credit. Two mints of 5 and 3 followed by one burn of 8: unlock succeeds, so a delta that moves between two nonzero values is counted once. Inside one unlock: settleFor without payment succeeds, clear of 1 with a zero delta reverts with 0xbda73abf, mint, take and burn of 2^127 revert with 0x93dafdf1 (SafeCastOverflow), a take of amount 0 in the codeless currency succeeds, sync of the codeless currency reverts without data, and a nested unlock reverts with 0x5090d6c6. These results describe the deployed contracts, which are other bytecode than a build of this checkout.

cleared.check: Deployed PoolManagers, read-only: is the lock closed when unlock returns, and does settle reset the synced currency (the two statements that the tests pin only without --isolate).
cleared.result: Same words on all 21 endpoints. Inside the callback exttload of the lock slot returns 1. After sync of the stub, which answers balanceOf with a fixed word, exttload of the currency slot returns the stub address; after settle, which returns 0, the slot returns 0, and a second settle returns 0. With a second stub that makes two more calls after unlock has returned, in the same eth_call: exttload of the lock slot returns 0 and take reverts with 0x54e3ca0d (ManagerLocked).

cleared.check: Lead L-217 for Unichain and the same walk on the other 20 networks, read-only with a stub that can attach value to inner calls (state override of code and balance).
cleared.result: Same words on all 21 endpoints. After sync of a token stand-in, settle with value 1 reverts with 0xb0ec849e (NonzeroNativeValue). After sync(address(0)), settle with value 1 returns 1 and the delta slot of the stub for address(0) reads 1. clear of 2 reverts with MustClearExactPositiveDelta. take of 1 native unit to the stub succeeds and the delta reads 0. mint of 5 raises balanceOf(stub, id) to 5, the delta reads -5 and the nonzero count reads 1; burn of 5 returns all three to 0. The synced currency guard of collectProtocolFees was tested on the eight networks that have a fee controller; Unichain has none, so that item of the lead cannot be tested there. On Tempo the value steps ran because the state override gave the stub a native balance. Whether an account can hold a native balance there was a question of earlier cycles, and this probe does not answer it. The Avalanche endpoint answered with a rate limit page once and gave the same words on the rerun.

cleared.check: Unpinned statements that stand against assumption A1 (src/PoolManager.sol:112, 113, 305, 310): can an ordinary account use them on any of the 21 networks.
cleared.result: No path in the text. Line 112 reads the transient counter that every _accountDelta call maintains (src/PoolManager.sol:368-378) and line 113 writes the lock slot; both hold for a caller as long as transient storage lives for exactly the transaction and rolls back with a reverted frame. settleFor and clear carry the same modifier as take and settle, so a locked manager rejects them. The feature that would break these lines is a transaction boundary inside or across user calls (protocol batches, system calls, nested runs with an empty transient map), which is the per network question of assumption A1 that earlier cycles answered from client source and simulation. The reading adds nothing that depends on a network. The cycle 3 critic probe showed on all 21 RPC nodes that these slots are scoped by address and that a second transaction reads zero where simulation is offered.

cleared.check: Unpinned statements that stand against assumption A2 (src/PoolManager.sol:360, 361, 364): a balance that falls between sync and settle, a balance rise credited twice, and a balance reading of 2^127 or more.
cleared.result: As written, a fall makes the checked subtraction revert, the reset after settle means a rise is credited once, and a rise of 2^127 or more reverts in toInt128. An ordinary account can still book a rise that a third party or the token itself causes between its own sync and settle, which is the class of F-041 and its variants and needs no unpinned line. I found no way to use these three statements beyond that class.

cleared.check: Unpinned statements that stand against assumptions A4 and A7 (src/types/Currency.sol:48, 64-74, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152, 166): a currency or hook address without code or at a precompile, and the gas forwarded to a native recipient.
cleared.result: A take of a currency whose address returns success and no data debits the caller and moves nothing, so the caller loses and no one else does; a credit in such an id needs sync, which reverts when balanceOf returns no data (confirmed on all 21 deployed contracts in the probe above for an address without code). A hook answer shorter than 32 bytes is rejected. A native payout forwards all gas to the recipient, which is lever P1 of ASSUMPTIONS.md and was swept per network in earlier cycles (F-021, F-047, F-048, F-049). These lines give an ordinary account no way to take or lock funds of others in the text as written.

cleared.check: Unpinned statement that stands against assumption A8 (src/PoolManager.sol:335): burn takes claims from a named account and credits msg.sender.
cleared.result: burn calls _burnFrom, which requires msg.sender to be the holder, an operator of the holder, or to have an allowance of at least the amount for that id (src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22). The credit goes to msg.sender, so the only question a network can change is who msg.sender is. A caller identity that the chain forges (aliased cross domain senders, system callers) would still need the holder's approval for that identity. On all 21 deployed contracts a burn of another address's claims by an unapproved caller gave no credit.

leads.question: Compile this checkout with solc 0.8.26 and the settings of foundry.toml on a machine that has the compiler, then run the three read-only probes in research/network-risk/cycles/006/core-code-test-pins.work (probe.py, probe2.py, probe3.py) against the built runtime bytecode placed by state override at an unused address on each of the 21 RPC endpoints. Do the 16 words of probe3, the lock and reset words of probe2 and the guard words of probe match the answers recorded for the deployed contracts?
leads.why: Every behaviour test so far ran against the contracts deployed today, which are other bytecode than a build of this checkout. The repository's tests as the CI runs them would pass without the end check of unlock, without the lock close and without the reset of the synced currency. The probes test exactly those statements and need no comparison of code copies. The immutable address in NoDelegateCall must be set to the override address when the runtime code is prepared.

leads.question: Does any hook test under test/ move one delta slot from a nonzero value to another nonzero value and then complete the unlock or assert the count, so that the condition previous == 0 at src/PoolManager.sol:375 is pinned?
leads.why: This unit found no such case in the router and ActionsRouter tests and did not trace every hook test. An increment on every nonzero result would block callers that touch one currency twice, which is a freeze without a theft.

leadResults.answer: Answered by reading and recorded as the info finding of this file plus eight cleared items with the test that pins each statement. Pinned by no test: removal of the CurrencyNotSettled check (src/PoolManager.sol:112); the lock guard on settleFor and clear (305, 310); the toInt128 limit at manager level (294, 313, 326, 334, 364); the use of _burnFrom in burn (335); the id truncation in mint and burn (324, 333); the checked subtraction for a fallen balance (360); empty return data, the 32 byte minimum and the missing code check in the token transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74); the gas of a native payout (Currency.sol:48); the length checks on hook answers (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152, 166); the missing lock check in collectProtocolFees. Pinned only when a test runs as one transaction, which the CI flag --isolate prevents: the lock close (113) and the reset of the synced currency (361). Each statement reads as its comment and error name require. Network features: A1 for 112, 113, 305 and 310; A2 for 360, 361 and 364; A4 and A7 for the Currency and Hooks lines; A8 for 335. None gives an ordinary account a path in the text as written.

Same answer as L-314. The lines that no test pins are listed there with the assumption each one stands against. The two places L-260 named as known (transfer to a currency without code, native fee collection while a native face is synced) are confirmed as unpinned, and the exemption of address(0) in src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 is in fact required by a test: without it test_collectProtocolFees_nativeToken_accumulateFees_gas would revert, because an empty currency slot equals the native currency.

Ran the behaviour test on the Unichain predeploy and on the other 20 PoolManagers with a stub placed by state override. Unichain at blocks 64690717, 64690913 and 64691062 gave the same words as Ethereum: NonzeroNativeValue for settle with value after a token sync, a credit of msg.value after sync(address(0)), zero for a settle without payment, ManagerLocked for take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint and burn while locked, MustClearExactPositiveDelta for a clear that is not exact, mint and burn moving the delta and the claim by the same amount, CurrencyNotSettled for an unpaid mint, the lock closed after unlock returns and the synced currency reset by settle. Not tested on Unichain: the synced currency guard of collectProtocolFees, because the fee controller there is the zero address.
